text:
anita: Hi team — I'm onboarding and hitting an issue with kubectl contexts. I ran `aws sso login --profile redwood-dev` then `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev-cluster --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-dev` but kubectl still shows context `arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev` that expects a role I don't have. Any pointers? Thanks!

joel: @anita you probably need the SSO role mapping. Run `aws sts get-caller-identity` to confirm what role you're assuming. Check `~/.kube/config` for the `exec` block too — it shows which profile/role the kubeconfig uses.

anita: how do I actually get the role? I looked at the onboarding checklist but the specific role name isn't listed.

joel: Submit an infra access request (https://redwood.example.com/access) and pick "eks: dev cluster - role". New hires usually auto-approve. Meanwhile, try `aws sso login --profile redwood-dev` again and then `aws eks get-token --cluster-name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-dev` — if that returns a token JSON you're good. If not paste your `exec` block here.

anita: paste snippet: ```users:\n- name: arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev\n  user:\n    exec:\n      apiVersion: client.authentication.k8s.io/v1alpha1\n      command: aws\n      args:\n      - "eks"\n      - "get-token"\n      - "--cluster-name"\n      - "redwood-dev"\n      - "--region"\n      - "us-west-2"\n      env:\n      - name: AWS_PROFILE\n        value: redwood-dev```

joel: Yea that's the SSO helper. If the token has expired you'll see a 403. Do `aws sso login --profile redwood-dev` then `aws eks get-token --cluster-name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-dev` — it should print the token. After that `kubectl config use-context arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev` or create a short alias: `kctx dev-redwood`. Also consider `aws-sso` cached creds — if you use a token manager (aws-vault / sso session) it helps.

priya: Also FYI our infra team often gives new hires a namespaced rolebinding instead of cluster-admin. In the access form request "namespace: anita-dev" and role `dev-edit` if you just need to iterate on apps. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: infra-access request received for anita at 1934567900 — request id #A-4821. ETA: 2 hours.

anita: Thanks everyone — after the access request was approved `aws sso login` + `aws eks get-token` fixed it. I can `kubectl get pods -n anita-dev` now. Posting the tiny function I added to my dotfiles for quick context switches: `function kctx(){ kubectl config use-context "${1:-$(kubectl config current-context)}" }` — hope this helps future new hires.
